key_insight: None of the audited pretrained shape completion models produced implantable cranial reconstructions, even when outputs looked convincingly skull-like.
clinical_relevance: These models, used as released, did not meet the geometric requirements for cranial implant placement.
method: Audited three public pretrained models, including two foundation models, zero-shot.
Compared outputs with the patient's remaining bone as a do-nothing baseline.
Checked whether predictions added material without intersecting existing bone.
evidence_signal: Across 210 carved defects and 29 real cases, no audited model output was implantable; a task-specific volumetric comparator selected on these cases was implantable in all but one.
watch_item: At the evaluated point densities, implant thickness could not be determined from the point-cloud outputs, limiting their suitability for implant design.
paper_title: Plausible but Unimplantable: A Trustworthiness Audit of Shape Completion Foundation Models for Cranial Defect Reconstruction
